in_arabic.name: حنفي
in_arabic.meaning: المذهب الحنفي الإسلامي أو الشخص المنتمي للمذهب الحنفي
in_arabic.long_meaning: الحنفي هو اسم يعود إلى المذهب الإسلامي الحنفي، أحد المذاهب الأربعة الرئيسية في الإسلام. يعتبر المذهب الحنفي واحدًا من المذاهب الفقهية الإسلامية الكبرى، ويتبعه العديد من المسلمين حول العالم. تأسس هذا المذهب على يد الإمام أبي حنيفة النعمان بن ثابت في القرن الثامن الميلادي. يتميز هذا المذهب بتفسيراته الفقهية وآرائه في مختلف مسائل الحياة اليومية والشؤون الدينية.

in_urdu.name: حنفی
in_urdu.meaning: حنفی مذهب یا حنفی مکتب فکر کا پیروکار
in_urdu.long_meaning: حنفی نام اسلامی مذهب حنفی سے منسلک ہے، جو اسلامی فقہ کے四大 مذاہب میں سے ایک ہے۔ یہ مذهب امام ابو حنیفہ نعمان بن ثابت نے سن ۸ویں صدی میں قائم کیا تھا۔ حنفی مذهب کے پیروکار دنیا بھر میں پائے جاتے ہیں، خاص طور پرجنوب ایشیا، مشرق وسطی اور افریقا میں۔ یہ مذهب اسلامی فقہ اور روزمرہ امور کے حوالے سے تفصیلی ہدایات فراہم کرتا ہے۔

in_hindi.name: हनफी
in_hindi.meaning: हनफी मजहब या हनफी विचारधारा का अनुयायी
in_hindi.long_meaning: हनफी नाम हनफी मजहब से जुड़ा है, जो इस्लामी न्यायशास्त्र के चार प्रमुख मजहबों में से एक है। इस मजहब की स्थापना आठवीं शताब्दी में इमाम अबू हनीफा नुएमान बिन ثابت द्वारा की गई थी। हनफी मजहब के अनुयायी दुनिया भर में पाए जाते हैं, खासकर दक्षिण एशिया, मध्य पूर्व और अफ्रीका में। यह मजहब इस्लामी न्यायशास्त्र और दैनिक जीवन के मामलों पर विस्तृत मार्गदर्शन प्रदान करता है।

in_pashto.name: حنفي
in_pashto.meaning: د حنفي مذهب پيروکار يا حنفي فکرۍ لارښود
in_pashto.long_meaning: حنفي نوم د حنفي مذهب سره تړلی دی، کوم چې د اسلامي فقه څلور لوی مذاهبو څخه يو دی. دا مذهب د اتمې پېړۍ په لومړيو کې د امام ابو حنيفه نعمان بن ثابت لخوا تاسیس شو. د حنفي مذهب پيروکار په ټوله نړۍ کې موندل کيږي، په ځانګړي ډول په جنوبي اسيا، منځني ختيځ او افريقيا کې. دا مذهب د اسلامي فقه او د ورځني ژوند د چارو په اړه تفصيلي لارښوونې وړاندې کوي.

in_english.name: Hanfi
in_english.meaning: Follower of the Hanafi school of thought in Islam
in_english.long_meaning: Hanfi refers to a person who adheres to the Hanafi school of thought, one of the four major Islamic jurisprudential schools. The Hanafi school was founded by Imam Abu Hanifa in the 8th century. Hanafi Muslims are found worldwide, particularly in South Asia, the Middle East, and Africa. The Hanafi school provides detailed guidance on Islamic jurisprudence and daily life matters, playing a significant role in shaping the religious and cultural practices of Muslims globally.

data.cultural_impact: The Hanafi school of thought, to which the name Hanfi holds reference, is one of the oldest and most widely practiced schools of Islamic jurisprudence. Originating in the late 7th century, it was founded by Imam Abu Hanifah (602-670 CE). Hanafi scholars contributed significantly to Islamic scholarship and jurisprudence, developing principles of Islamic law and shaping the Muslim community's legal and religious practices. Hanafis are found in various regions of Asia, Europe, and the Middle East, with a significant presence in both the Indian subcontinent and Central Asia. Despite its geographical spread and diversity, it has maintained a strong cultural and intellectual identity, contributing to the richness and diversity of Muslim tradition. Importantly, Hanafi legal and ethical principles continue to inform contemporary Muslim discourses and debates on matters ranging from familial relationships, commerce, and social justice.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Hanfi has deep spiritual significance, derived from the root h-n-f, meaning 'to love'. It serves as a constant reminder for the bearer to adhere deeply and devotedly to the teachings and practices of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). Implicit in this commitment is a profound reverence and respect for the Prophet's teachings and conduit of divine wisdom. Hanfi, therefore, implies an individual's unwavering dedication to seeking the pleasure of Allah, enlivened by a heart governed by a deep love and obedience towards the Prophet. It serves as a daily reminder for the Hanafi to strive in the path of love and devotion, seeking a spiritual growth that draws them closer to Allah and propels them forward on their journey towards self-realization.

historical_references.context: Al-Shafi'i was a renowned Islamic scholar and is considered the founder of the Shafi'i school of Islamic jurisprudence. The Hanafi, Maliki, and Shafi'i schools are the three main Sunni schools, each named after their founders. Al-Shafi'i was born in Yemen but spent most of his life in Egypt. Hanafi is one of the other major Islamic legal schools, and it is believed that the name may be derived from Abu Hanifah, the founder of the Hanafi school, although this is not universally accepted.

modern_usage.modern_context: The term 'Hanafi' is used in modern contexts to refer to the Islamic legal tradition founded by Imam Abu Hanifa in the 8th century. Hanafi scholars and their followers continue to contribute to the scholarship of Islamic law, engaging in academic debate and interpretation of legal texts. Hanafi legal thought is also visible on social media platforms, where individuals and communities discuss and share information related to Hanafi jurisprudence. In the legal practice sphere, Hanafi jurisprudence is applied in courts and institutions throughout the Muslim world and beyond.
